data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'gaos', meaning 'stranger' or 'foreigner'. In the New Testament, this name is given to a centurion who has faith in Jesus' healing power. The name Gaivn carries the meaning “Stranger, Foreigner” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gaivn usually hope their child will grow to embody stranger, foreigner and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey of faith and embracing the unknown.
data.etymology: Gaivn belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Stranger, Foreigner.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gaivn total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gaivn highlights the universality of the Christian faith, as seen in the Greek origin of the name and its association with a Roman centurion who believed in Jesus' power.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gaivn can serve as a reminder of the inclusivity and reach of God's love, extending beyond cultural and geographical boundaries, just as it did for the centurion in the New Testament. It also symbolizes the faith and openness of the centurion, emphasizing that even those considered outsiders or foreigners can have deep spiritual connection and belief.
